title: Peace Be to This Habitation
description: Peace Be to This Habitation in Tonic Solfa to LUX EOI, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 924 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Domestic Worship”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens Double (8.7.8.7.8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to LUX EOI; any other Eights and Sevens Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Peace be to this ha-bi-ta-tion; Peace to all that dwell there-in; Peace, the ear-nest of sal-va-tion; Peace, the fruit of par-doned sin; Peace, that speaks the heav-enly Giv-er; Peace, to world-ly minds un-known; Peace di-vine, that lasts for-ev-er; Peace, that comes from God a-lone.

lines: Peace to all that dwell therein;
Peace, the fruit of pardoned sin;
Peace, that speaks the heavenly Giver;
Peace, that comes from God alone.
Jesus, Prince of Peace, be near us;
Fix in all our hearts thy home;
With thy gracious presence cheer us;
Give our favored souls to prove
In the realms of bliss above.

licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to LUX EOI by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
